body:
The response formatters write every JSON token straight into Kestrel's response `PipeWriter`, which takes a lock on each `GetSpan` and `Advance`, so a response pays thousands of lock operations.

Every formatter now writes through a `ChunkedPipeBufferWriter`: a 64 KB buffer that is copied to the pipe when it is full or the formatter flushes. The buffer is rented on the first write and returned as soon as it is copied, before the flush is awaited, so a stream holds nothing between events. A write of 4 KB or more goes to the pipe directly. The writer is cached per thread, so a response allocates nothing it did not allocate before. Flush points are unchanged: single results flush once at the end, streams per event.

### Benchmarks

Results are written into a plain pipe and into a pipe that locks on every buffer call like Kestrel's response writer. The 10 KB and 47 KB results are the gateway benchmark response with one and ten users, as a single result, a batch of five and an event stream of five. The small results are product lists from 292 bytes to 5.6 KB, and the ones below 4 KB also run as a batch of five and an event stream of five. The scalar results are four pre-encoded UTF-8 strings of the given size, written the way Fusion writes source result strings.
